payload.author: AJV20
payload.title: Add safe config.yaml viewer

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Pulled this into a read-only worktree and read the new `api/routes.py` code plus the `_redact_text` chain in `api/helpers.py` it leans on. The read-only-viewer design is the right risk posture, and the path-based masking is sound. I found one concrete leak gap and two things worth confirming.

## Concrete gap: numeric/bool secrets bypass path redaction

In `_redact_config_for_display` the scalar passthrough runs **before** the sensitive-path check:

```python
if value is None or isinstance(value, (bool, int, float)):
    return value
text = str(value)
if any(fragment in path_text for fragment in sensitive_fragments):
    return "[REDACTED]" if text else text
return _redact_text(text)
```

So a credential stored as a number under a sensitive key — e.g. a numeric `token`, a PIN, a Telegram `chat_id`, or `api_key: 1234567890` if YAML coerces it to int — returns in cleartext, because `isinstance(value, (int, float))` short-circuits and never reaches the `path_text` test. The fix is to check the path first for any non-container scalar:

```python
if isinstance(value, (dict, list)):
    ...  # recurse as today
if any(fragment in path_text for fragment in sensitive_fragments):
    return "[REDACTED]" if value not in (None, "") else value
if value is None or isinstance(value, (bool, int, float)):
    return value
return _redact_text(str(value))
```

That way a sensitive key path is masked regardless of the value's type.

## The second net is setting-gated — worth a doc line

The "non-secret strings still pass through the existing redactor" net calls `_redact_text` (`api/helpers.py:334`), which early-returns when `api_redact_enabled` is false:

```python
if not _enabled:
    return text
```

The path-based `[REDACTED]` in this PR is unconditional (good — it fires even with redaction disabled), but the value-level net for tokens accidentally pasted into *non-secret* keys silently becomes a no-op when an operator has turned redaction off. That's a reasonable design, just worth a one-line note in the panel/help text so nobody assumes the viewer scrubs unknown-key secrets when `api_redact_enabled: false`.

## Minor: the endpoint returns the absolute config path

`/api/config/safe` returns `"path": str(cfg_path)`, which ships the server's absolute config path (e.g. a home-dir path) to the browser. `filename` already covers what the UI needs to display. For an authenticated settings panel this is low-risk, but dropping `path` (or returning just the basename) avoids leaking host filesystem layout into client-side state and copy-paste.

## On the tests

`tests/test_safe_config_viewer.py` covers string masking, the GET-only/read-only contract, and the frontend mount well. The mock at `monkeypatch.setattr(routes, "_redact_text", ...)` confirms the second net is invoked only for non-secret strings (`assert "***" not in calls`) — nice. Adding a case like `{"providers": {"x": {"token": 12345}}}` and asserting it becomes `[REDACTED]` would lock in the numeric-secret fix above.

Net: solid, low-blast-radius slice. The numeric-secret ordering is the one I'd want addressed before merge since the whole point of the viewer is to never ship a credential to the client.

payload.title: Add manual session title regeneration

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Pulled the branch into a read-only worktree and read the `api/routes.py` + `api/streaming.py` hunks against `origin/master`. The structure is clean: the new `generate_session_title_for_session` helper (`api/streaming.py`) correctly reuses `_first_exchange_snippets` / `_latest_exchange_snippets`, `_generate_llm_session_title_via_aux`, the fallback chain, and wraps the aux-model call in `profile_env_for_background_worker` (`api/profiles.py:688`) for profile isolation — all of which exist on master, so the wiring checks out. Saving with `touch_updated_at=False` to avoid reordering the sidebar is the right instinct.

Two things worth addressing.

## 1. Same `state.db` write-through gap as #3225
The handler persists the regenerated title to the WebUI JSON store only:

```python
# api/routes.py — /api/session/title/regenerate
with _get_session_agent_lock(sid):
    s.title = str(next_title).strip()[:80] or "Untitled"
    s.llm_title_generated = True
    s.save(touch_updated_at=False)
publish_session_list_changed("session_title_regenerate")
```

There's no push to the agent's `state.db`, so for a bridged/CLI session the TUI keeps showing the stale `/title`. This is exactly the gap #3225 documents for `/api/session/rename`. The only existing path that writes a title through is the post-turn block at `api/routes.py:9991-10008`:

```python
if load_settings().get("sync_to_insights"):
    from api.state_sync import sync_session_usage
    sync_session_usage(
        session_id=s.session_id, ...
        title=s.title,
        profile=getattr(s, 'profile', None),   # #2762 parity
    )
```

Mirroring that here (guarded on `sync_to_insights`, passing `profile=` for #2762 parity) would make regenerate land in `state.db` immediately rather than waiting for the next turn. Worth coordinating with #3225 so `rename` and `regenerate` share one write-through helper instead of two near-duplicates.

## 2. Read-only guard message vs. HTTP semantics
The guard rejects imported/read-only sessions with a 403 (`"Read-only imported sessions cannot be renamed"`) — good. But note `bad(handler, msg, 404)` is used for "Session not found" while the 422 path returns `"Could not generate a better title"`. That 422-on-empty-title is a reasonable choice, just confirm the frontend in `static/sessions.js` surfaces it distinctly from the 403 (an imported session and a transient LLM miss are very different UX cases — one should disable the menu item, the other should offer retry).

## Minor
- `generate_session_title_for_session` accepts an `agent=None` param that's only forwarded to `_generate_llm_session_title_via_aux`; confirm the aux helper actually spins one up when `None`, otherwise the manual path may be paying first-call init cost the background refresh path avoids.
- The diff adds a blank-line cluster (`+\n\n\n`) before the new helper in `api/streaming.py`; trivial, just tidy on rebase.

Solid first slice for #3106. The title-generation reuse is the right call; the main blocker before merge is the `state.db` write-through so regenerate doesn't reproduce the #3225 cross-surface drift.

payload.body:
Re-reviewed at head `dc0d470b`. Pulled the refreshed branch into a worktree and re-read the regenerate handler in `api/routes.py` plus the new menu wiring in `static/sessions.js`. The main blocker from my last pass is resolved correctly.

## Resolved: #1 state.db write-through

`8f9b34dd` added `_sync_session_title_to_insights()` (`api/routes.py:5649`) and the regenerate handler now calls it after the JSON save:

```python
with _get_session_agent_lock(sid):
    s.title = str(next_title).strip()[:80] or "Untitled"
    s.llm_title_generated = True
    s.save(touch_updated_at=False)
_sync_session_title_to_insights(s)   # routes.py:5708
```

The helper mirrors through `sync_session_usage(..., title=session.title, profile=getattr(session, "profile", None))` guarded on `sync_to_insights` — exactly the shape of the post-turn block at `api/routes.py:10215`, with the `profile=` parity for #2762. This closes the cross-surface drift I flagged against #3225. Good.

## Residual: menu gate vs server guard are asymmetric

The server guard rejects both flags:

```python
if getattr(s, "read_only", False) or getattr(s, "is_imported", False):
    return bad(handler, "Read-only imported sessions cannot be renamed", 403)
```

But the only frontend gate that suppresses the menu item is the early return at `static/sessions.js:2167`, which keys off `_isReadOnlySession(session)` — and that helper (line 918) checks only `read_only`/`is_read_only`:

```js
return !!(session && (session.read_only || session.is_read_only));
```

So a session with `is_imported: true` but `read_only: false` still renders the "Regenerate title" action, and clicking it always 403s into the `catch` toast. It's a narrow case, but the server code explicitly treats `is_imported` as distinct from `read_only`, so the frontend should too — either fold `is_imported` into `_isReadOnlySession` (cleanest, since rename shares that gate) or gate the new `menu.appendChild` on it. Right now rename and regenerate disagree about which sessions are eligible.

## Cosmetic nits (non-blocking)

- The rename block's close collapsed to `));  }` (`sessions.js:2196`) — the brace lost its own line in the merge. Harmless, just untidy.
- The new regenerate `menu.appendChild(...)` is indented 4-6 spaces while every sibling action in `_openSessionActionMenu` uses 2. JS doesn't care, but it stands out in the file.

Net: the merge-blocker is genuinely fixed and the write-through matches the existing insights-sync contract. I'd align the `is_imported` gate before merge so the menu doesn't surface an action that's guaranteed to fail for imported-but-writable sessions; the cosmetic items can ride along on the same touch. CI is green across all shards.

payload.title: Add pinned MCP tool shortcuts

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Pulled this into a read-only worktree and read the full `_renderMcpTools` / shortcut helpers in `static/panels.js` against `origin/master`. The feature design is good — pinning to `localStorage` and inserting a composer prompt instead of calling a tool directly (the test even asserts `"/api/mcp/call" not in PANELS_JS`) is the right low-risk slice for #3042. But there's a concrete bug that makes the Use/Pin buttons and the shortcut chips non-functional in the rendered DOM.

## Blocker: JSON-quoted arg collides with the double-quoted `onclick` attribute

`_mcpToolShortcutJsArg` produces a **double-quoted** string:

```js
function _mcpToolShortcutJsArg(value){
  return JSON.stringify(String(value||'')).replace(/</g,'\\u003c');
}
```

`JSON.stringify("srv::tool")` → `"srv::tool"` (with the surrounding double quotes). That value is then interpolated straight into a double-quoted attribute:

```js
<button ... onclick="insertMcpToolShortcut(${_mcpToolShortcutJsArg(toolKey)})">
```

so the rendered HTML is:

```html
<button onclick="insertMcpToolShortcut("srv::tool")">
```

The first inner `"` terminates the `onclick` attribute. The browser parses `onclick="insertMcpToolShortcut("` — a syntax-error fragment — and treats `srv::tool")"` as garbage attributes. Clicking Use / Pin / a shortcut chip does nothing (throws `SyntaxError` in the inline handler). The helper escapes `<` but never escapes the `"` that actually breaks the attribute. All three call sites are affected (`Use`, `Pin/Unpin` in the tool row, and the chip `onclick` in `_renderMcpToolShortcuts`).

## Why CI is green anyway

`test_mcp_tool_rows_have_use_and_pin_buttons_with_safe_js_args` only asserts the literal **source string** is present:

```python
assert "onclick=\"insertMcpToolShortcut(${_mcpToolShortcutJsArg(toolKey)})\"" in PANELS_JS
```

It never renders the template or parses the resulting DOM, so a quoting bug that only manifests after HTML parsing slips straight through. Worth keeping in mind for the test bar here.

## Fix

The simplest fix matches what every other handler in this file already does — single-quote the JS literal and let `esc()` (`static/ui.js:158`) entity-encode it. Compare the existing MCP toggle at `static/panels.js:7703`:

```js
onclick="toggleMcpServer('${encodedName}',${!isEnabled})"
```

`esc` encodes `'` → `'` and `"` → `"`, so a single-quoted literal can't break out of either the JS string or the attribute. So drop `_mcpToolShortcutJsArg` and use:

```js
onclick="insertMcpToolShortcut('${esc(toolKey)}')"
...
onclick="toggleMcpToolShortcut('${esc(toolKey)}')"
```

If you'd rather keep the helper, it needs to HTML-encode the quotes JSON introduces too, e.g. `JSON.stringify(...).replace(/</g,'\\u003c').replace(/"/g,'"')` — then the browser decodes `"` back to `"` inside the attribute and the call survives. Either works; the `esc`-with-single-quotes form is more consistent with the rest of `panels.js`.

## Smaller notes

- `_mcpToolShortcutKey` joins `server::name` with `::`; a server or tool name containing `::` could in theory alias two keys, but that's a corner case and pinning is per-user local state, so it's not a blocker.
- The i18n coverage is thorough — `test_mcp_tool_shortcut_i18n_keys_exist_in_all_locale_blocks` verifies all 7 keys land in every locale block, which is the right bar.

Net: nice feature, correct execution model (no direct tool call). The attribute-quoting bug is the one merge-blocker — right now the buttons render but don't fire. A render/DOM-level assertion (or a tiny jsdom click test) would catch this class of bug that the source-string check can't.

payload.body: Pulled the branch into a read-only worktree and read `static/ui.js` at HEAD plus `origin/master` around the MEDIA restore pass (`renderMd`, `static/ui.js:3459-3540`). The artifact-card approach is sound — using inline-flex `` wrappers keeps the markup valid inside markdown paragraph context, and routing the preview through `api/media?path=...` preserves the existing auth gate. Two concrete issues worth addressing before merge. ## 1. Hardcoded English labels bypass i18n The new `localArtifactCard` helper emits literal `Open` / `Download` strings: ```js // static/ui.js (this PR) Open Download ``` Everything else in this same function localizes via `t(...)` — e.g. `static/ui.js:3489` and `:3507` use `t('media_svg_label')`, and `:3517` uses `t('pdf_loading')`. These two action labels should go through `t('media_open')` / `t('media_download')` (add the keys to `static/i18n.js`), otherwise non-English locales get stray English in every generated-image card. Your own test `test_local_image_media_uses_artifact_card` asserts `"Open"` / `"Download"`, which will need updating to match the localized output. ## 2. `inline=1` / `download=1` query params are no-ops on this route `localArtifactCard` builds: ```js const openUrl=src+(...?'&':'?')+'inline=1'; const downloadUrl=src+(...?'&':'?')+'download=1'; ``` But `src` here is the `api/media?path=...` URL, which is served by `_handle_media` (`api/routes.py:8001`). That handler only inspects `inline` for *preview* types (PDF/audio/video, `:8108`) — for image MIME it already serves `disposition=inline` regardless, and it **never reads `download`**. The `download=1` param is honored only by the *other* handler at `api/routes.py:8301` (`force_download = qs.get("download",[""])[0] == "1"`), which is the workspace-artifact path, not `/api/media`. So the actual download is driven entirely by the anchor's `download="${safeName}"` attribute (same-origin, so it works), and both query params are dead weight that may mislead future readers. Recommend dropping them, or wiring `_handle_media` to honor `download=1` so the two paths behave consistently. ## Minor This PR and #3219 both insert code immediately after the `mediaPlayerHtml` closure (`static/ui.js:~3468`) and both add an `[Unreleased]` block to `CHANGELOG.md`, so they'll conflict on merge — whichever lands second will need a rebase. Lightbox interaction is fine: the click handler at `static/ui.js:652` does `e.target.closest('.msg-media-img')`, and the card still nests ``, so click-to-zoom continues to work and the new Open/Download anchors sit outside that target.

Both items from my last pass are resolved correctly, and the renderer-extraction edge case you hit on CI is handled well. ## Both prior items resolved **i18n (item #1):** the action labels now route through `t(...)` and the keys exist in every locale — `media_open`/`media_download` added to en (`Open`/`Download`), it (`Apri`/`Scarica`), ja (`開く`/`ダウンロード`), ru (`Открыть`/`Скачать`), es (`Abrir`/`Descargar`). That's a clean way to satisfy the shard without weakening the localized browser path. Worth a one-line code comment noting *why* the fallback exists (extracted-renderer test context), so a future reader doesn't mistake it for a missed localization and "simplify" it back into a hardcode. ## Confirmations - Lightbox still works: the card nests ``, and the zoom handler at `static/ui.js:652` keys off `.msg-media-img`, so click-to-zoom is intact and the Open/Download anchors sit outside that target. - The CSS test (`test_generated_artifact_card_css_defined`) locks in `.msg-artifact-card/-meta/-title/-actions/-action`, so the card styling can't silently regress. payload.title: fix: consolidate client disconnect handling — single source of truth for error tuple

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Pulled the branch into a read-only worktree and read the full diff against `origin/master` (`api/helpers.py`, `server.py`, and the test file — read-only, not executed).

The core idea is good: factoring the response-write path through `_safe_write()` and wrapping the 500-fallback `j()` so a disconnect during error generation can't cascade into a second traceback. The nested handler in `do_GET`/`_handle_write` is the right shape:

```python
except Exception:
    print(f'[webui] ERROR {self.command} {self.path}\n' + traceback.format_exc(), flush=True)
    try:
        j(self, {'error': 'Internal server error'}, status=500)
    except _CLIENT_DISCONNECT_ERRORS:
        pass
```

Two things to reconcile before merge.

## 1. The PR description overclaims the `handle_error` part

The body says it "Added `QuietHTTPServer.handle_error()`", but that already exists on master (`server.py:204-220`) and this diff doesn't touch it. Master's version already swallows `ConnectionResetError, BrokenPipeError, ConnectionAbortedError, TimeoutError` plus `OSError` errnos 32/54/104/110. Worth correcting the description so reviewers know the server-loop layer is unchanged — the new coverage here is purely the per-response `_safe_write` + 500-fallback wrapping.

## 2. Duplicate `_CLIENT_DISCONNECT_ERRORS` with diverging membership

`api/routes.py:48` already defines its own tuple:

```python
_CLIENT_DISCONNECT_ERRORS = (
    BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, ConnectionAbortedError,
    TimeoutError, OSError,
)
```

The new one in `api/helpers.py` is the same minus `OSError` plus `ssl.SSLError`. Since `ssl.SSLError` subclasses `OSError`, the `routes.py` tuple already catches SSL errors via the broad `OSError` arm, while the new `helpers.py` tuple enumerates `ssl.SSLError` explicitly but drops the bare `OSError` catch-all. Now `server.py` imports the `helpers` one and `routes.py` keeps its own — two tuples with different semantics for "what counts as a disconnect." That will drift. Suggest defining it once (in `helpers.py`) and having `routes.py` import it, picking one membership policy. If you intend to keep the broad `OSError` arm, add it to the helpers tuple; if you want to be narrow, drop `OSError` from routes too — but make it a single source of truth.

## Minor

`github-search-report.md` (53 lines, dated 2026-05-26) reads like research scratch output. Probably belongs in the PR description or a gist rather than committed to the repo root.

Net: the response-write hardening is a reasonable incremental improvement over the existing `handle_error` layer. Fix the description claim and de-duplicate the error tuple, and this is in good shape. I did not run the test suite (cron policy is read-only inspection of PR branches).

## 2. `_CLIENT_DISCONNECT_ERRORS` — consolidated

Single source of truth established:

- **Definition**: `api/helpers.py` — now uses `OSError` (which covers `ssl.SSLError` since it subclasses `OSError`). Added a docstring comment explaining the inheritance relationship and listing the specific errno values caught (32 EPIPE, 54 ECONNRESET, 104 ECONNABORTED, 110 ETIMEDOUT).
- **Consumer**: `api/routes.py` — removed the 13-line duplicate definition, added `_CLIENT_DISCONNECT_ERRORS` to the existing `from api.helpers import (...)` block at line 1033.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks @hayriodabas — this is two good optimizations in one PR, and I reviewed both deeply.

**Shipping the Docker-cache half now** (v0.51.177, via #3207): building the image once and caching layers via `type=gha`, with variants restoring from cache. I kept your structure and made one tweak — the variant restore uses `cache-from` only (dropped the redundant `cache-to` re-export; `build-image` is the sole writer). Verified on the PR's own CI: the `build-image` cache job + `Smoke single` both pass restoring from cache.

**Deferring the test-sharding half** with a tracking issue (#3208). The sharding is genuinely appealing — I confirmed the partition is clean (3 shards = 6903 tests, no loss/overlap) and the ~66% speedup is real (one shard ran in ~38s vs ~180s sequential). But when I ran the shards for real (each with its own isolated port + state dir, so not a collision artifact), a handful of tests that pass in the full sequential run fail when sharded — they depend on shared module-level/server state set up by sibling tests (e.g. `test_onboarding_status_defaults_incomplete`, `test_title_aux_routing`, `test_ctl_script`). Shipping sharding onto an order-dependent suite would make CI flaky.

#3208 captures the path to fix the suite's shard-safety (fixture isolation on the order-dependent tests), after which we can adopt your `tests.yml` sharding as-is. Closing this PR since the Docker half ships separately and the sharding half is tracked in #3208 — really appreciate the contribution, the speedup work is valuable and we'll get the sharding in once the suite is ready for it.

payload.title: fix: guard session cache ownership across compression

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Reviewed read-only against `origin/master` (`79145c0a`); I read the full `get_session` flow and all four `streaming.py` touch points plus the new tests. This is a careful, well-scoped defensive layer — the invariant "the cache key must agree with the cached object's own `session_id`" is the right framing, and it's enforced consistently across every place compression/recovery can rotate lineage ids. Pairs naturally with the sidebar-side dedupe in #3192.

## get_session eviction (api/models.py:2202-2217)

The insertion sits right after the LRU `move_to_end`, before the `metadata_only` branch, so it guards both load paths:

```python
if str(getattr(cached, 'session_id', '') or '') != str(sid):
    ...
    with LOCK:
        if SESSIONS.get(sid) is cached:
            SESSIONS.pop(sid, None)
    cached = None
```

Two things I checked that make this safe: the `SESSIONS.get(sid) is cached` re-check under `LOCK` is correct double-checked locking — it won't pop a fresh object another thread installed between the unlocked read and the eviction. And setting `cached = None` falls through to the normal disk reload + re-cache, which `test_get_session_evicts_cached_object_with_wrong_session_id` confirms (`models.SESSIONS["requested-tip"] is loaded` afterward). The metadata-only variant correctly leaves the cache empty per the docstring contract at `models.py:2196-2201`, and the second test pins that.

## Compression migration (api/streaming.py:5489-5506)

The old `SESSIONS[new_sid] = SESSIONS.pop(old_sid)` blindly trusted that the object under `old_sid` belonged there. The new code installs the live continuation object `s` under `new_sid` directly and only restores `old_sid` if the popped object actually self-identifies as `old_sid`:

```python
cached_old_session = SESSIONS.pop(old_sid, None)
if cached_old_session is not None and cached_old_session is not s:
    cached_old_sid = str(getattr(cached_old_session, 'session_id', '') or '')
    if cached_old_sid == str(old_sid):
        SESSIONS[old_sid] = cached_old_session
    ...
SESSIONS[new_sid] = s
SESSIONS.move_to_end(new_sid)
while len(SESSIONS) > SESSIONS_MAX:
    SESSIONS.popitem(last=False)
```

One observation worth confirming: master's version was net-neutral on cache size (pop one, add one). The new code can net-add an entry (it may re-insert `old_sid` *and* add `new_sid`), which is why the `SESSIONS_MAX` trim loop was added — good catch, and `move_to_end(new_sid)` before the trim guarantees the just-installed continuation is the most-recently-used so the `popitem(last=False)` can never evict it. The only nuance: a restored `old_sid` is inserted *without* a `move_to_end`, so it's the eviction candidate if the cache is at cap — which is the right priority (the live tip matters more than the archived snapshot).

## Agent-cache identity helper (streaming.py:3692-3717)

`_cached_agent_matches_session` returning `True` for `identity is None` is the right backwards-compat choice — old/fake agents without a `session_id`/`_session_db` stay reusable rather than being force-evicted. The fallback chain (`session_id` → `_session_id` → `_session_db.session_id`) is covered by `test_cached_agent_session_identity_matches_requested_sid`, including the legacy and db-owned cases. The cache-hit path (`:4823`) cleanly defaults `agent = None` and only the verified-reuse branch sets it, with the `register_agent` block correctly guarded by `if agent is not None`.

## Steer path (streaming.py:6404-6413)

`test_handle_chat_steer_evicts_mismatched_cached_agent` asserts the exact `{"accepted": False, "fallback": "no_cached_agent", "stream_id": None}` fallback and that the bad entry is dropped — so a mismatched agent degrades to the interrupt fallback instead of steering the wrong conversation. Correct.

No blockers from my read. The source-invariant test (`test_compression_cache_migration_never_moves_unverified_cached_object_to_new_sid`) pins the three key string changes so a future refactor can't silently re

payload.author: ai-ag2026
payload.title: fix: keep tool cards anchored during history paging

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

Read the full diff at this PR's HEAD against `origin/master` — `api/routes.py` `_tool_calls_for_message_window`, the new `_syncToolCallsForLoadedMessages()` in `static/sessions.js`, and the three call sites (`_ensureMessagesLoaded`, `_loadOlderMessages`, `_ensureAllMessagesLoaded`). The root-cause analysis is correct and matches what I see on master: the fallback rebuild in `static/ui.js:6672` only fires when `S.toolCalls` is empty, so after `_loadOlderMessages` swaps `S.messages` the stale `rawIdx` anchors are never refreshed. Resyncing on every window replacement is the right fix, and centralizing it in one helper is cleaner than #3186's inlined branches.

One concern: the legacy (session-level `tool_calls`) path now rebases the index **twice**.

## Code reference

Backend rebase (this PR, `api/routes.py`):

```python
if start_idx <= assistant_idx < end_idx:
    rebased = dict(tool_call)
    rebased["assistant_msg_idx"] = assistant_idx - start_idx
    filtered.append(rebased)
```

Frontend rebase (this PR, `static/sessions.js` `_syncToolCallsForLoadedMessages`):

```js
const idx=copy.assistant_msg_idx;
if(Number.isInteger(idx)&&idx>=offset&&idx<offset+msgs.length){
  copy.assistant_msg_idx=idx-offset;
}
```

Both run with the *same* `start_idx` / `_messages_offset`. The backend already converts to window-relative coordinates, then the frontend subtracts `offset` again.

## Diagnosis

The single-tool-call test passes only by luck. In `tests/test_session_tail_payload.py::test_msg_before_window_keeps_only_that_page_session_tool_calls`, offset=1 and the one in-window call rebases to `assistant_msg_idx=0`; on the frontend `0 >= offset(1)` is false, so the second subtraction is skipped. Add a *second* in-window tool call and it breaks:

- Legacy session, `session.tool_calls = [{idx:1},{idx:2}]`, request `msg_before=3&msg_limit=2` → window `messages[1:3]`, `_messages_offset=1`.
- Backend rebases → `[{idx:0},{idx:1}]`.
- Frontend with `offset=1`, `msgs.length=2`: idx0 stays 0 (`0>=1` false) ✓; idx1 → `1>=1 && 1<3` true → `1-1=0` ✗.

Both cards now anchor to `rawIdx 0` (`static/ui.js:6415` matches `tc.assistant_msg_idx` against `renderedRawIdxs`), so the second tool card collapses onto the first row and the one expected on `messages[2]` disappears — the same "tool calls disappear" class this PR targets, just for legacy sessions during mid-transcript paging.

## Recommendation

Pick one coordinate authority. Since the backend change makes `/api/session` emit window-relative indices, the frontend should treat the server list as **already relative** and drop the offset arithmetic in `_syncToolCallsForLoadedMessages` — keep only `S.toolCalls = sessionToolCalls.map(tc => ({...tc, done:true}))` in the legacy branch. The offset subtraction is only correct if the backend keeps absolute indices (the #3186 approach), and you can't have both.

## Test plan

Extend `test_msg_before_window_keeps_only_that_page_session_tool_calls` with two in-window legacy tool calls (`assistant_msg_idx` 1 and 2) and assert the payload yields distinct rebased indices `0` and `1`. Then, since the JS resync isn't exercised by Python string-match tests, add a DOM/JSDOM check (or a focused assertion in the JS test harness) that two legacy cards in a paged window render against two different `rawIdx` rows rather than collapsing. The current `tests/test_tool_call_history_paging.py` is a source-string presence check, so it won't catch the double-rebase.

(For reference: #3186 takes the client-only route and adopts the server's indices verbatim; that avoids the double-rebase but leaves legacy windowed sessions misanchored by `+offset` because master's backend still ships absolute indices. The two PRs are solving the same bug from opposite ends — worth converging on one.)

payload.title: fix: hash dirty WebUI dev builds

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Reading `_dirty_suffix()` at `api/updates.py:184` on `origin/master` plus the diff, this is a minimal, well-targeted improvement for #3159 that preserves the fast-path the function was designed around.

## The problem on master

`_dirty_suffix` uses `git diff-index --quiet HEAD --` purely as a boolean dirty probe, then returns a constant marker:

```python
out, ok = _run_git(['diff-index', '--quiet', 'HEAD', '--'], path, timeout=timeout)
if ok:
    return ""
...
if not out or out.startswith('git exited with status '):
    return "-dirty"
return ""
```

So every dirty dev build emits the same `-dirty` suffix — `static/foo.js?v=<tag>-dirty` stays byte-identical across successive local edits, and browsers keep serving the cached asset. The fix hashes the actual tracked diff only after the cheap probe has already confirmed dirtiness:

```python
if not out or out.startswith('git exited with status '):
    diff, diff_ok = _run_git(['diff', '--binary', 'HEAD', '--'], path, timeout=timeout)
    if diff_ok and diff:
        digest = hashlib.sha1(diff.encode('utf-8', errors='replace')).hexdigest()[:8]
        return f"-dirty-{digest}"
    return "-dirty"
```

Now `?v=<tag>-dirty-<sha1[:8]>` changes whenever tracked content changes, giving a reliable per-edit cache-busting signal.

## Why this is the right slice

- The expensive `git diff --binary` only runs on the already-confirmed-dirty branch, so clean builds keep the single `diff-index --quiet` cost and the early `if ok: return ""` fast path is untouched.
- `_run_git` returns `(detail, False)` on timeout / missing git (`api/updates.py:159`), so `diff_ok` is `False` and the code falls back to the plain `-dirty` marker rather than blocking version display — matching the function's "never block on git" contract.
- `hashlib` is already imported at `api/updates.py:11`, so no new dependency.

## Scope note

As the PR says, the hash covers only tracked changes vs `HEAD` (`git diff HEAD`), so untracked new files won't shift the suffix — but that's consistent with the existing `diff-index ... HEAD --` probe scope, so there's no behavior asymmetry introduced. Worth keeping in mind for a brand-new untracked asset, though that's an edge case for dev workflows and out of scope here.

`test_version_badge.py` → 29 passed and CI is green on 3.11/3.12/3.13. The mocked + real-temp-repo coverage proving the suffix changes across edits is the right verification. LGTM.

payload.author: ai-ag2026
payload.title: fix: handle Windows media and turn journal edge cases

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Reading the diff at `api/turn_journal.py` and `api/routes.py` against `origin/master`, both fixes match the root-cause analysis in #3170 and #3171 precisely, and the regression tests target the right failure modes.

## Turn-journal fix (#3170)

On master, `append_turn_journal_event()` referenced `os.O_DIRECTORY` directly:

```python
try:
    dir_fd = os.open(path.parent, os.O_DIRECTORY)
    ...
except OSError:
    pass
```

The constant doesn't exist in `os` on native Windows, so the `AttributeError` is raised at attribute-lookup time, *before* `os.open` runs — and `except OSError` never catches it. The PR guards it correctly:

```python
o_directory = getattr(os, "O_DIRECTORY", None)
if o_directory is not None:
    try:
        dir_fd = os.open(path.parent, o_directory)
        ...
    except OSError:
        pass
```

The file write + `os.fsync(fh.fileno())` above this block is untouched, so per-file durability is preserved on POSIX; only the directory-fd fsync (which Windows has no equivalent for) is skipped. `test_append_turn_journal_event_skips_directory_fsync_without_o_directory` uses `monkeypatch.delattr(os, "O_DIRECTORY", raising=False)` to simulate Windows and asserts the journal file is still written — exactly the right shape.

## Media cross-drive fix (#3171)

The master check called `commonpath` inside the generator:

```python
within_allowed = any(
    _os.path.commonpath([str(target), str(root)]) == str(root)
    for root in allowed_roots
    if root.exists()
)
```

On Windows, `ntpath.commonpath` raises `ValueError: Paths don't have the same drive` when `target` is on `D:` and a root is on `C:`, which aborts the whole `any(...)` → request 500. The new `_path_is_within_root()` helper isolates each comparison:

```python
def _path_is_within_root(child: Path, root: Path) -> bool:
    try:
        return os.path.commonpath([str(child), str(root)]) == str(root)
    except ValueError:
        return False
```

So a cross-drive root is treated as a non-match and the loop continues to the next allowed root (or the per-session MEDIA token path), instead of crashing. The allow-list isn't weakened — a `D:` file still needs `MEDIA_ALLOWED_ROOTS` or a session token to actually be served; this only stops the 500 before that check is reached.

## One small note

The helper uses module-level `os` (`api/routes.py:12`), while the surrounding `_handle_media` body uses a locally-imported `import os as _os` alias in several spots (e.g. `:7902`, `:8059`). Both resolve to the same module so it's correct, but if you want stylistic consistency with the rest of that function you could alias inside the helper too. Not blocking.

CI is green on 3.11/3.12/3.13. Both changes fail closed on unsupported platforms rather than crashing request/turn handling — clean, well-scoped fixes. LGTM.

payload.title: fix: close evicted agents from WebUI cache

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Reading the diff at `api/streaming.py` against `origin/master` plus the agent-side contract in `run_agent.py` and `gateway/run.py`, this is a well-scoped fix and the refactor is faithful. A few notes after walking the lifecycle end to end.

## What the fix actually buys us

The old eviction block (`api/streaming.py:4880-4903` on master) committed memory and closed `_session_db`, but never tore down the memory provider:

```python
_lifecycle_commit(_evicted_sid, agent=_evicted_agent, wait=True)
if not _lifecycle_has_uncommitted_work(_evicted_sid):
    _lifecycle_unregister_agent(_evicted_sid)
...
if _should_close_evicted_agent and ... _evicted_agent._session_db is not None:
    _evicted_agent._session_db.close()
```

The new helper adds the missing step:

```python
shutdown_memory_provider = getattr(agent, 'shutdown_memory_provider', None)
if callable(shutdown_memory_provider):
    shutdown_memory_provider()
```

That routes into `AIAgent.shutdown_memory_provider` (`run_agent.py:2231`), which calls `_memory_manager.shutdown_all()` → `provider.shutdown()` per provider (`memory_manager.py:612-621`). That is exactly where a Hindsight-style provider closes its aiohttp `ClientSession`, so the "unclosed client" warning the PR targets is real and this is the correct teardown point. It also mirrors the agent's own gateway path, which calls `shutdown_memory_provider` in `_cleanup_agent_resources` (`gateway/run.py:3604-3619`), so WebUI eviction now matches gateway session-expiry semantics. Good.

## One subtlety worth confirming (probably benign)

`on_session_end()` now fires twice on eviction: once inside `commit_memory_session()` and again inside `shutdown_memory_provider()` (both call `_memory_manager.on_session_end(...)` — `run_agent.py:2241` and `:2265`). I checked whether that double-fire is a hazard:

- WebUI's `commit_session_memory` invokes `effective_agent.commit_memory_session()` with no messages (`api/session_lifecycle.py:166`), so `on_session_end([])` already runs with an empty transcript. The helper's `shutdown_memory_provider()` is also no-arg, so the second `on_session_end([])` is empty too. Providers that re-extract on `on_session_end` see `[]` both times, and the base hook is a no-op (`memory_provider.py:165`), so this should be harmless.
- Note this diverges slightly from gateway, which passes `agent._session_messages` to `shutdown_memory_provider(...)` to preserve the real transcript for `on_session_end` (`gateway/run.py:3617`, ref #15165). WebUI doesn't, but since the commit step already drove extraction, the empty second call is redundant rather than lossy. Calling it out in case you want the eviction path to feed `_session_messages` for parity.

## Dirty-eviction path: no regression

When commit leaves `has_uncommitted_work() == True`, the helper sets `should_close_evicted_agent = False` and skips **both** `shutdown_memory_provider()` and `session_db.close()`. That preserves retryability for the dirty segment and matches the pre-PR behavior (master also gated `_session_db.close()` on `_should_close_evicted_agent`), so `test_lru_eviction_closes_evicted_agent_session_db` and the new still-dirty test stay consistent. No fd-leak regression introduced.

## Tests

`test_streaming_agent_cache_lifecycle.py` covers both branches (clean → commit+unregister+shutdown+close; dirty → provider kept alive), and the source-invariant updates in `test_memory_session_lifecycle_generation.py` / `test_v050259_sessiondb_fd_leak.py` correctly re-anchor on the helper. Assertions match the implemented behavior.

LGTM on substance. The only optional follow-up is passing `_session_messages` into `shutdown_memory_provider()` for gateway parity, but as-is it's safe.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks for turning the gateway-parity follow-up around. Reading the new head at `api/streaming.py` against the prior diff, the change lands exactly where the earlier review pointed.

## What changed since the last pass

The eviction helper now feeds the cached transcript into provider shutdown instead of an empty no-arg call (`api/streaming.py`, `_close_evicted_agent_at_session_boundary`):

```python
shutdown_memory_provider = getattr(agent, 'shutdown_memory_provider', None)
if callable(shutdown_memory_provider):
    session_messages = vars(agent).get('_session_messages', [])
    shutdown_memory_provider(session_messages)
```

This mirrors the gateway cleanup contract. On the agent side `gateway/run.py:3615-3619` does the same handoff:

```python
session_messages = getattr(agent, "_session_messages", None)
if isinstance(session_messages, list):
    agent.shutdown_memory_provider(session_messages)
else:
    agent.shutdown_memory_provider()
```

and `AIAgent.shutdown_memory_provider(self, messages=None)` at `run_agent.py:2231` forwards `messages or []` into `_memory_manager.on_session_end(...)` and the context engine. So a provider whose `on_session_end(messages)` re-extracts now sees the real transcript on eviction, matching gateway session-expiry semantics. That closes the divergence flagged last round.

## On `vars(agent).get(...)` vs `getattr(...)`

Using `vars(agent).get('_session_messages', [])` rather than `getattr` is a reasonable choice here, but note it diverges slightly from gateway's `getattr` + `isinstance(list)` shape. For a real `AIAgent` the attribute lives in `__dict__` (set at `run_agent.py:1518`), so they're equivalent. The practical difference shows up only with `MagicMock` stubs, where `getattr` would hand a truthy child mock to `on_session_end` and `vars().get` correctly yields `[]` — which is what your `test_evicted_agent_lifecycle_shutdown_uses_empty_messages_when_missing` asserts. Functionally fine; just flagging that a non-dict `__slots__` agent (none exist today) would behave differently from the gateway path. If you want byte-for-byte parity you could match gateway's `getattr` + `isinstance` guard, but it's not blocking.

## Dirty-eviction branch

Confirmed the still-dirty path is unchanged: when `has_uncommitted_work()` stays `True`, `should_close_evicted_agent` is set `False` and **both** `shutdown_memory_provider()` and `session_db.close()` are skipped, preserving retryability. `test_evicted_agent_lifecycle_keeps_provider_alive_when_commit_still_dirty` locks that, and the fd-leak invariants in `test_v050259_sessiondb_fd_leak.py` re-anchor on the helper correctly.

LGTM. CI is green across 3.11/3.12/3.13. The `vars().get` note is optional.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

Read the diff at PR #3139 (`fix/picker-provider-qualified-no-fuzzy-snap`) plus `static/ui.js` and the new tests on the PR branch. The fix is narrowly scoped and correct: once exact-and-provider-aware lookup fails, provider-qualified inputs (`@provider:model` or any `vendor/model` slash form) short-circuit to `null` instead of falling through to prefix/substring fuzzy matching. That kills the original #3113 snap from `xiaomi/mimo-v2.5` → `xiaomi/mimo-v2.5-pro` without disturbing the bare-root prefix case the existing regression suite (#1188) protects.

## Code reference

`static/ui.js:1086-1092` (PR HEAD), inserted between the exact-match branch and the prefix/substring branch:

```js
  // If the request is provider-qualified (either explicit @provider:model or
  // a slash-qualified vendor/model id), do NOT fuzzy-match a sibling model
  // once exact/provider-aware lookup failed. Returning null lets the caller
  // preserve the raw typed value instead of snapping to the closest catalog
  // entry. ...
  if(rawModel.startsWith('@')||rawModel.includes('/')) return null;
```

The provider-aware exact lookup directly above (`norm(o.value)===target && _getOptionProviderId(o).toLowerCase()===preferred`) still resolves the legitimate cases, so an actually-cataloged `@openrouter:xiaomi/mimo-v2.5` would return its option value. Only the uncatalogued path falls through to `null`.

## Caller behavior on null

I traced every consumer to confirm a `null` from `_applyModelToDropdown` does the right thing on the provider-qualified path:

- `static/sessions.js:509-518` — appends a custom `<option>` carrying `dataset.provider=sessionProvider` and re-applies. That preserves the typed value on the active session.
- `static/boot.js:1683-1692` — falls through to `_ensureModelOptionInDropdown`, which is the explicit "append-and-select raw modelId" path at `static/ui.js:1111-1130`.
- `static/ui.js:1718-1719` (chat-side picker entry) — same `_ensureModelOptionInDropdown` fallback.
- `static/onboarding.js:487` and `static/messages.js:556,561` — ignore the return value, which is fine because onboarding/effective-model flows feed catalog ids the exact branch already handles.

So the "preserve raw typed selection" promise in the PR description holds on every persistence path I checked.

## Test coverage

`tests/test_issue1188_fuzzy_match.py:128-152` adds two regression tests. The negative case (`test_explicit_provider_hint_does_not_snap_to_sibling_model`) uses `vendor/special-model` against a catalog that only contains `vendor/special-model-pro` and asserts `None`; the positive case asserts exact provider-qualified hits still resolve. Both line up with the new short-circuit. The harness was also extended to forward `preferredProvider` and to shim `_getOptionProviderId` (lines 48-58 of the diff), which is needed because the production function early-returns once the provider-aware exact match succeeds.

## One small follow-up worth considering

The new guard treats *any* slash in `rawModel` as provider-qualified. That's correct for the OpenRouter/vendor case, but it means a bare typed `gpt/4o` (hypothetical, no provider intent) also short-circuits past the prefix branch. Probably fine — `gpt/4o` isn't a real id pattern and the cost of being strict here is small — but it's worth noting in the changelog as the intentional behavior so future users typing odd `a/b` strings don't get surprised. Not a blocker.

CI is green across 3.11/3.12/3.13. LGTM.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

Read the diff on PR #3138 plus `api/streaming.py` (the home of `_WEBUI_PROGRESS_PROMPT`), `api/routes.py:_handle_chat_sync` (the new prompt-injection callsite), and `agent/conversation_loop.py` on the agent side to confirm what the prompt actually does. The change is correct in spirit and small: one extra bullet in the WebUI progress guidance forbidding scratchpad fragments like "Need check logs", and a re-export so the otherwise-unused sync chat path gets the same guidance. The test additions assert the new strings end up in the ephemeral prompt build.

## Code reference

`api/streaming.py:199-211` (PR HEAD):

```python
_WEBUI_PROGRESS_PROMPT = """
WebUI progress guidance:
- ...
- Do not include terse planning fragments or scratchpad shorthand in visible
  assistant text. Avoid fragments like "Need check logs", "Need inspect
  email", or "maybe invite"; either omit them or rewrite them as clear
  user-facing progress.
- For direct answers or very short tasks, skip progress updates and answer normally.
""".strip()
```

And the new sync-path injection at `api/routes.py:9628-9651`:

```python
from api.streaming import (
    _WEBUI_PROGRESS_PROMPT,
    ...
)
workspace_system_msg = (
    f"Active workspace at session start: {s.workspace}\n"
    ... existing workspace tag instructions ...
    "Never fall back to a hardcoded path when this tag is present.\n\n"
    f"{_WEBUI_PROGRESS_PROMPT}"
)
```

## Diagnosis

Two observations worth raising before merge — neither is a blocker.

**1. Streaming vs sync path use different injection mechanisms.** In the streaming path the progress prompt is set on `agent.ephemeral_system_prompt` (`api/streaming.py:4955`), which `agent/conversation_loop.py:966-967` appends to the *effective* system every turn but never persists. In the sync path it's now baked into `workspace_system_msg`, which is passed as `system_message` to `run_conversation` and on first turn ends up in `agent._cached_system_prompt = agent._build_system_prompt(system_message)` (`agent/conversation_loop.py:286-288`), which then gets persisted into the session DB's `system_prompt` column via `_restore_or_build_system_prompt`. So a session started on the sync path persists the progress guidance into the prefix cache row; a streaming session does not. The two paths converge for behavior but diverge for caching semantics. In practice the sync endpoint is documented as "Fallback synchronous chat endpoint (POST /api/chat). Not used by frontend." (`api/routes.py:9551`), so the divergence is mostly theoretical. If you ever want parity, the cleaner shape is to also set `agent.ephemeral_system_prompt` on the sync path instead of inlining into `system_message`.

**2. The guard is purely a prompt-level instruction.** The PR description acknowledges this and that's correct — there's no output sanitizer. Models that ignore the instruction will still emit "Need inspect email" as visible text. The PR is the right *first* fix (cheapest place to enforce), but expect to need a small bounded sanitizer (regex-match a leading "Need <verb>" or "maybe <noun>" fragment at the start of a visible delta and either drop it or treat it as scratchpad). Worth filing as a follow-up issue rather than expanding this PR.

## Test coverage

`tests/test_webui_surface_context.py:25-27` covers the streaming path through `_webui_ephemeral_system_prompt`, asserting the three new strings:

```python

assert "Need inspect email" in prompt
assert "clear user-facing progress" in prompt
```

That confirms the prompt builder includes the new bullet, but it doesn't exercise the sync path's `workspace_system_msg` construction. A quick parallel test that builds the sync workspace message and asserts `_WEBUI_PROGRESS_PROMPT in workspace_system_msg` would lock the import-side of the sync change in too. Cheap to add.

payload.author: AJV20
payload.title: fix: add Joplin search auth compatibility

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

Read the PR diff plus surrounding helper `api/routes.py:_joplin_api_get` and its three call sites (`/search` at `api/routes.py:13012`, `/notes/{id}` at `:13043` and `:13157`). The fix is narrow, correct, and partially walks back the May 25 hardening commit `dc868415` ("fix: send joplin token in auth header") that moved every Joplin call to header-only auth. That commit broke local Web Clipper builds whose `/search` rejects header-only auth with HTTP 403; this PR restores compatibility *only* for `/search` while preserving header auth for `/notes/{id}` and any future endpoints.

## Code reference

`api/routes.py:12969-12978` (PR HEAD):

```python
safe_path = "/" + str(path or "").lstrip("/")
query = dict(params or {})
# Joplin Web Clipper builds can reject header-only auth on /search even when
# they accept it elsewhere. Keep the Authorization header for defense in
# depth and add the query token only for /search compatibility.
if safe_path == "/search":
    query["token"] = token
url = f"{base_url}{safe_path}?{urlencode(query)}"
request = Request(url, headers={"Authorization": f"token {token}"})
```

The path normalization above the guard (`"/" + str(path or "").lstrip("/")`) means callers like `_joplin_api_get("/search", ...)` and `_joplin_api_get("search", ...)` would both hit the branch. All three current call sites pass literal paths starting with `/search` or `/notes/`, so the equality check is reliable.

## Diagnosis

The compatibility evidence in the PR body (local `/search` returns 403 with header-only, 200 with query token) is consistent with the upstream Joplin Web Clipper changelog around the search route. The narrowing to `safe_path == "/search"` is the right shape — broader endpoints don't need it, and keeping the query token off `/notes/{id}` retains the original mitigation that motivated `dc868415`.

Two small notes:

**1. Token still ends up in URL for `/search`.** That's intentional and acknowledged in the comment, and for a 127.0.0.1 Web Clipper the risk surface (URL leakage via referers, server-side access logs, proxy headers) is essentially zero. Worth checking though that nothing in the WebUI ever logs `request.full_url` or `request.get_full_url()` from a Joplin response — quick grep on the worktree confirms nothing in `api/routes.py` does that. Clean.

**2. Path-equality could be a touch more lenient.** If Joplin ever adds `/search/<subpath>` (it currently doesn't), the strict `safe_path == "/search"` skips the shim. `safe_path.startswith("/search")` would future-proof at zero cost. Not a blocker.

## Test coverage

`tests/test_webui_notes_sources.py:141-200` adds two regression tests:

- `test_joplin_api_get_sends_header_and_query_token_for_clip_search_compat` — calls `/search`, asserts both `token=secret-token` is in the URL *and* the `Authorization` header is `token secret-token`. This locks in the dual-auth shape.
- `test_joplin_api_get_keeps_non_search_token_out_of_url` — calls `/notes`, asserts `token=` is NOT in the URL. This locks in the narrowing — the previous test on master conflated both behaviors into one assertion and was harder to read.

Both assertions match the production code. The header-only-on-non-search regression test pair is what you want here.

## Independence from PR #3135

I confirmed PR #3135 (external-notes guardrails) does not touch `_joplin_api_get` — it modifies `api/streaming.py` and the durable-write surface context only. There is no merge conflict and no overlap on the auth transport. The split is clean and the order of merge between #3135 and #3137 doesn't matter.

CI is green across 3.11/3.12/3.13. The change is bounded to a single helper, well-tested, and reverses the right slice of a prior fix. LGTM.

payload.author: zapabob
payload.title: Detect shared OpenCode API key in WebUI

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

Read the diff plus the agent-side provider registry and the WebUI's existing env-var aliasing layer. The intent (let a single shared `OPENCODE_API_KEY` enable both OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go provider groups in the picker) is reasonable on its face, but the change is **WebUI-only and creates a UI/runtime mismatch** unless a parallel agent change lands too. As shipped, this would make the picker happily show OpenCode Zen and Go models for users who set only `OPENCODE_API_KEY` — and inference would then fail at runtime because the agent runtime never reads that env var.

## Code reference

WebUI side, `api/config.py:3481-3485` (PR HEAD):

```python
if all_env.get("OPENCODE_ZEN_API_KEY") or all_env.get("OPENCODE_API_KEY"):
    detected_providers.add("opencode-zen")
if all_env.get("OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY") or all_env.get("OPENCODE_API_KEY"):
    detected_providers.add("opencode-go")
```

Agent side, `hermes_cli/auth.py:365-385` (read-only, unchanged):

```python
"opencode-zen": ProviderConfig(
    id="opencode-zen",
    ...
    api_key_env_vars=("OPENCODE_ZEN_API_KEY",),
    base_url_env_var="OPENCODE_ZEN_BASE_URL",
),
"opencode-go": ProviderConfig(
    id="opencode-go",
    ...
    api_key_env_vars=("OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY",),
    base_url_env_var="OPENCODE_GO_BASE_URL",
),
```

A `grep -rn OPENCODE_API_KEY ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/` returns zero hits. The agent has no notion of a shared OpenCode bridge key today.

## Diagnosis

There is an established WebUI/agent contract for env-var aliasing (`api/providers.py:680-695`):

```python
_PROVIDER_ENV_VAR_ALIASES: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {
    # #1500 — agent runtime reads LM_API_KEY (canonical), but WebUI builds
    # ≤ v0.50.272 wrote LMSTUDIO_API_KEY into .env. Keep reading both.
    "lmstudio": ("LMSTUDIO_API_KEY",),
}
```

That mechanism is the right shape for "the agent canonical is X, but we should also accept Y". But the comment is also the point: aliases work because both names eventually resolve to the **same agent-side runtime**. For OpenCode, there are two distinct providers with different base URLs (`https://opencode.ai/zen/v1` vs `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`), and the agent code reads two distinct env vars. Adding `OPENCODE_API_KEY` to the WebUI detection set without an agent runtime change means:

1. User sets `OPENCODE_API_KEY=...` only.
2. WebUI picker shows OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go groups (this PR).
3. User picks `glm-4.6` (a Go model). Chat fires.
4. Agent's `_resolve_api_key` for `opencode-go` reads only `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY`, finds nothing, surfaces "no API key for provider opencode-go". Hard failure.

So the fix has to land on the agent side first, either by extending `api_key_env_vars=("OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY", "OPENCODE_API_KEY")` (and same for zen) in `hermes_cli/auth.py`, **or** by the WebUI also writing `OPENCODE_API_KEY` into both `OPENCODE_ZEN_API_KEY` and `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` at process startup so the agent's strict lookup succeeds. The first is the cleaner shape since it lives in the same `ProviderConfig.api_key_env_vars` tuple that already supports fallback (see `anthropic` line 314 with three valid names, or `google` line 237 with two).

## Other observations

- The two unrelated `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` changes in `tests/test_opencode_providers.py` are fine — they make Windows-on-non-UTF8-locale runs pass. Worth keeping even if the main change is reworked.
- The author mentions CI was not run upstream (`statusCheckRollup: []` confirms; their local runs were Windows). Upstream CI would not catch this — there are no tests that exercise the WebUI→agent runtime boundary with `OPENCODE_API_KEY` only.

## Recommendation

Hold this PR until either:

1. The agent's `PROVIDER_REGISTRY` is extended (`api_key_env_vars=("OPENCODE_ZEN_API_KEY", "OPENCODE_API_KEY")` and the matching Go entry), **or**
2. The WebUI gains an aliasing-on-write path in `api/providers.py` that mirrors `OPENCODE_API_KEY` into both canonical env vars when set.

Option

payload.author: AJV20
payload.title: fix: harden external notes guardrails

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

Read the PR head (`cron-pr-3135`) against `origin/master` — the diff is two unrelated changes bundled together:

1. **Joplin auth transport change** (`api/routes.py:_joplin_api_get`): switches `Authorization: token <X>` header → `?token=<X>` query parameter.
2. **Durable-notes guardrail extension**: expands the existing surface-context prompt and applies it to the sync chat path.

The guardrail piece is fine on its own. The Joplin auth change is what I want to flag, because it directly reverts a defense-in-depth fix that landed only a few days ago.

## Code reference

The change replaces this body in `_joplin_api_get` (master, `api/routes.py:12961-12973`):

```python
safe_path = "/" + str(path or "").lstrip("/")
query = dict(params or {})
url = f"{base_url}{safe_path}?{urlencode(query)}"
request = Request(url, headers={"Authorization": f"token {token}"})
```

with (PR head, `api/routes.py:12969-12981`):

```python
query = dict(params or {})
# Joplin Web Clipper accepts the token as a query parameter for API routes.
# Some endpoints (for example /search) return 403 when the token is sent
# only via Authorization header, even though /ping may accept the header.
query["token"] = token
url = f"{base_url}{safe_path}?{urlencode(query)}"
request = Request(url)
```

That header form was added in commit `dc868415` ("fix: send joplin token in auth header", merged via PR #2894 a few days ago) precisely to address #2886 — the rationale in PR #2894's body was *"URLs are easy to leak through future logging or diagnostics. A request header is the narrower place for the token and keeps it out of the generated URL string."*

## Diagnosis

Three concerns:

1. **This reopens the leak vector #2886 closed.** Any future call site that logs `request.full_url`, any traceback that prints the URL, any proxy access log, any test capture (the new test `test_joplin_api_get_uses_query_token` literally asserts the token is now in `captured["url"]`) will surface the token. The docstring on `_joplin_api_get` still says *"Call the local Joplin Web Clipper API without logging credentials"* (`api/routes.py:12962`), which is no longer accurate — the credential is now in the URL string used by the request.

2. **The compatibility claim is asymmetric and shouldn't require a revert.** Joplin's Web Clipper has historically accepted **both** the `Authorization: token <X>` header and `?token=<X>` query parameter on the same endpoints; if `/search` is genuinely rejecting header-only auth on the version you're hitting, the safer fix is to send **both** — keep the `Authorization` header for narrow defense-in-depth, and also include `query["token"] = token` as a compatibility shim for clipper builds that drop the header. That preserves the #2886 fix on builds that honor the header while unblocking the ones that don't.

   ```python
   query = dict(params or {})
   query["token"] = token
   url = f"{base_url}{safe_path}?{urlencode(query)}"
   request = Request(url, headers={"Authorization": f"token {token}"})
   ```

   With this shape the existing #2886 mitigation still applies on any clipper version that honors the header, and `/search` works on the ones that don't. Worth verifying which Joplin/Web Clipper build actually returns 403 to header-only auth — pinning that in the changelog would help future maintainers.

3. **Docstring drift.** If the revert is intentional, please update the `_joplin_api_get` docstring on line 12962 — *"without logging credentials"* implies a guarantee the function no longer provides.

## Note on the second change

The durable-notes guardrail extension (`api/streaming.py:222-227`, `api/routes.py:_handle_chat_sync`) is a clean, well-scoped tightening of the existing prompt. Test additions in `test_webui_surface_context.py:23-25` line up with the new assertions. No concerns there.

## Test plan

- Confirm with the actual Joplin/Web Clipper build that returns 403 to header-only `/search` — capture the version string in the CHANGELOG en

payload.title: Fix #3018: preserve per-turn ephemeral fields (_turnUsage, _turnDuration, _gatewayRouting) across session refreshes

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Heads up: this PR overlaps with PR #3121 (lizhihao-99, opened ~3h before this one), which targets the same issue #3018 and uses the same general approach. Worth coordinating before merge.

Comparing the two:

**PR #3121** (lizhihao-99): patches `static/messages.js` only, two `S.messages=` sites in `attachLiveStream` (the cancel-recover branch and `_restoreSettledSession`). Identity-match by "last assistant message with `_turnUsage`" rather than by content prefix.

**This PR #3131**: patches `static/messages.js` and adds a third call site in `static/sessions.js:1322` (`_ensureMessagesLoaded` / `loadSession`). Identity-match by `(role, timestamp, content prefix)`.

Both diagnose the bug correctly. The diagnosis matches what's in `messages.js:1797-1969` (the `_finishDone` closure decorates `lastAsst._turnUsage`/`_turnDuration`/`_turnTps`/`_gatewayRouting`) and the three replace sites I see when I `grep -n "S\.messages=" static/messages.js static/sessions.js`:

```
messages.js:1848   inside _finishDone — replace then decorate (in-order, no preserve needed)
messages.js:2247   cancel-recover async fetch
messages.js:2299   _restoreSettledSession
sessions.js:1322   _ensureMessagesLoaded / loadSession
sessions.js:1477   nextMessages assignment (worth checking)
sessions.js:1559   second nextMessages site (worth checking)
```

This PR catches sessions.js:1322 which #3121 misses; #3121's hoisted module-level helper is cleaner than this PR's inner-closure definition. Best-of-both is to merge them.

## Bugs in this PR

### 1. Closure-scoped helper is unreachable from sessions.js

The `_carryForwardEphemeralTurnFields` function is defined **inside `attachLiveStream`**:

```js
function attachLiveStream(activeSid, streamId, uploaded=[], options={}){
  ...
  function _carryForwardEphemeralTurnFields(prevMessages, nextMessages){ ... }
  if(typeof window!=='undefined'){
    window._carryForwardEphemeralTurnFields=_carryForwardEphemeralTurnFields;
  }
  ...
```

The function is only assigned to `window._carryForwardEphemeralTurnFields` when `attachLiveStream` runs. `loadSession` / `_ensureMessagesLoaded` can run **before** any stream is attached (e.g. clicking a finished session from the sidebar on first load). At that point `window._carryForwardEphemeralTurnFields` is undefined, the `typeof` guard at sessions.js:1322 is `'undefined'`, and the carryforward silently no-ops.

The fix is to hoist the function to module scope, same as #3121 did after my review on that PR.

### 2. `(role, timestamp, content prefix)` identity key is fragile across the exact scenarios that trigger this bug

The renderer's stable-key approach uses `_message_identity` shape on the server (`api/streaming.py:_message_identity` keys on `(role, text, tool_call_id, _partial)`). This PR's `_messageIdentityKey`:

```js
function _messageIdentityKey(m){
  if(!m||!m.role) return '';
  const ts=m._ts||m.timestamp||'';
  let body='';
  if(typeof m.content==='string') body=m.content;
  else if(Array.isArray(m.content)){ ... }
  return `${m.role}|${ts}|${body.slice(0,160)}`;
}
```

The bug specifically fires when the SSE stream completes and a server refresh races in. In that exact window:

- `_ts` / `timestamp` on the client-side message may be the streaming-attach time; the server payload's timestamp is the server-write time (often a few seconds later when journal flushes happen). These don't match.
- During multi-part assistant messages (assistant text segments interleaved with tool calls), client may have separate message rows while server collapses them into one — content prefixes diverge.

The 160-char content prefix in particular fails for short replies ("OK", "Got it", "Continue") and for replies that share prefixes ("Here's the file:", "Here's the result:").

#3121's "last assistant with `_turnUsage`" identity is narrower but actually more robust for this specific bug — because by definition only one message has `_turnUsage` at the moment of decoration, and the lookup is just "

payload.author: Sanjays2402
payload.title: Fix #3076: don't force mobile send-on-Enter when a real keyboard is co-present

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
LGTM. The fix maps directly to the reporter's suggestion in #3076 ("Disable or refine the `_mobileDefault` auto-detection for devices with `(pointer: fine)` or when a physical keyboard is detected"). Reading the original gate at static/boot.js:1142 and the new helper:

## Code reference

Pre-PR gate (static/boot.js:1142):

```js
const _mobileDefault=matchMedia('(pointer:coarse)').matches
                  &&window._sendKey==='enter'
                  &&_isVirtualKeyboardLikelyOpen();
```

The bug: `(pointer:coarse)` is true on any touch-primary device, **whether or not** a physical keyboard is also attached. Android tablet + Bluetooth keyboard, Surface in tablet mode, iPad + Magic Keyboard all satisfy it. Combined with `_isVirtualKeyboardLikelyOpen()` (which uses a 120px viewport-shrink heuristic that browsers also trip on for IME hint chips, address-bar toolbars, gesture-bar insets), the mobile override fires when the user is typing on real keys.

The post-PR gate:

```js
const _mobileDefault=matchMedia('(pointer:coarse)').matches
  &&!_hasFinePointerCoexisting()
  &&window._sendKey==='enter'
  &&_isVirtualKeyboardLikelyOpen();
```

`_hasFinePointerCoexisting()` uses `matchMedia('(any-pointer:fine)')`. The `any-pointer` family checks across **all** available pointing devices on the system, so a coarse touchscreen + a fine Bluetooth mouse/keyboard/trackpad will satisfy `any-pointer:fine`, while a pure-touch phone won't.

## Browser support is fine

`(any-pointer: fine)` is Level 4 Media Queries, shipped in all evergreen browsers since 2017 (Chrome 41, Firefox 64, Safari 9, Edge 12). The PR wraps it in a try/catch defensively. The try/catch is overcautious — `matchMedia` itself doesn't throw on unknown queries (returns `MediaQueryList` with `matches:false`) — but it's harmless.

## Edge cases I traced

- **Pure-touch Android phone, software keyboard open**: `(pointer:coarse)` true, `(any-pointer:fine)` false → mobile default still kicks in ✓ (no regression)
- **iPad with Magic Keyboard**: `(pointer:coarse)` true, `(any-pointer:fine)` true (trackpad on the keyboard exposes fine pointer) → desktop semantics restored ✓
- **Android tablet + Bluetooth keyboard (no trackpad)**: depends on the browser's keyboard heuristics; Chrome on Android typically reports `(any-pointer:fine)` true when a HID keyboard is paired, even without a mouse, because the keyboard itself counts as a fine input device. Worth a sanity check on the reporter's exact setup, but matches the documented Media Queries spec.
- **Smart-TV with remote-as-pointer**: some setups expose the remote as a fine pointer (the PR body acknowledges this). For TV setups the failure mode is "desktop Enter sends instead of newline" — recoverable via the Settings `send_key` choice. Acceptable.

## One small note

The PR's risk section says "A touch-only device that ships with a 'fine' pointer (some smart-TV setups expose a remote as fine pointer) would lose the mobile default." Worth pinning the explicit setting in Settings as the documented escape hatch — `window._sendKey='ctrl+enter'` from boot.js:1525 honors user preference and bypasses `_mobileDefault` entirely. That's already in the file; no code change needed, but worth a note in the WebUI settings copy if regressions are reported.

payload.title: Fix #3103: stop emitting Connection: close on long-lived SSE streams (session-list reconnect loop)

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
The diagnosis is correct, but the fix is incomplete and the reasoning about HTTP semantics needs a small correction. Reading the introducing commit (598fd4ff "perf(http): enable HTTP/1.1 keep-alive" by Qi) plus all five SSE handlers in `api/routes.py`.

## What 598fd4ff actually did, and why the SSE handlers added the header

Commit message:

> Enable HTTP/1.1 on the WebUI server so browsers can reuse TCP connections across normal API/static requests. Tighten response framing by adding Content-Length to short manual responses and marking SSE/streaming responses as Connection: close, keeping HTTP/1.1 message boundaries unambiguous.

So the header was added deliberately — once the server upgraded to HTTP/1.1 with keep-alive by default, SSE bodies (which have no Content-Length and end with FIN) needed an explicit `Connection: close` to tell the client "this connection won't be reused, don't try to read another response after this body ends." Removing it without dealing with framing risks the browser keeping the socket pool entry around expecting another HTTP/1.1 response on the same connection.

That said, the symptom is real (#3103 documents a ~1s reconnect loop), so the underlying browser-side behavior with `Connection: close` on EventSource needs handling.

## The fix only patches 2 of 5 SSE handlers

Same class of bug exists at all five sites. `grep -n 'Connection.*close' api/routes.py` (master HEAD):

```
7231:        handler.send_header("Connection", "close")   # _handle_sse_stream (chat journal-replay branch)
7243:        handler.send_header("Connection", "close")   # _handle_sse_stream (chat live branch)
7374:        handler.send_header("Connection", "close")   # _handle_terminal_sse_stream
7452:        handler.send_header('Connection', 'close')   # _handle_gateway_sse_stream ← patched
7485:        handler.send_header('Connection', 'close')   # _handle_session_events_stream ← patched
8116:        handler.send_header('Connection', 'close')   # _handle_approval_sse_stream
8217:        handler.send_header('Connection', 'close')   # _handle_clarify_sse_stream
```

The PR only patches lines 7452 and 7485 (gateway + session-events). The chat stream at 7231/7243 is a much longer-lived connection (whole-message streaming, often minutes), and the terminal SSE at 7374 is open for the lifetime of a PTY. If the reporter's loop is in fact triggered by `Connection: close`, those handlers will have the same behavior; the bug isn't fixed for them.

## "Browsers treat Connection: close as one-shot" — overstated, but the loop is real

EventSource's reconnect behavior is documented to fire whenever the connection drops, regardless of `Connection: close`. The 1s loop you're seeing is more likely a function of:

1. `python BaseHTTPServer` is one-request-per-connection on each thread anyway, so the socket closes when the handler returns (true with or without the header).
2. `Connection: close` told the browser **not to bother with the keep-alive pool** for this socket, which combined with the server-side close means the EventSource sees an immediate clean close → fire `onerror` → schedule reconnect after the EventSource default backoff (~1s in Chrome's no-jitter case).
3. The first request returns from `_handle_gateway_sse_stream` quickly (e.g. when `watcher.subscribe()` returns before the worker has anything to push) → close → reconnect → repeat.

Removing `Connection: close` likely changes the timing because the browser keeps the socket warm in its pool, but the reconnect still happens when the socket actually closes. The real question is **why the server-side handler returns so quickly** that the loop is tight. Looking at `_handle_gateway_sse_stream` from origin/master:

```python
q = watcher.subscribe()
try:
    while True:
        try:
            event, payload = q.get(timeout=_SSE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS)
        ...
```

That loop only exits on exception (client disconnect) or break — there's no obvious "return immediately when watc

payload.title: Fix #3114: keep jump-to-question button on intermediate assistant messages

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
LGTM. Reading the diff against `static/ui.js:6360-6491` (where `questionRawIdxByAssistantRawIdx` is populated) + the rendering site at 6487-6493, the diagnosis is exactly right: the map is built for every visible assistant message (loop at 6378-6382, `else if(role==='assistant') questionRawIdxByAssistantRawIdx.set(entry.rawIdx,lastQuestionRawIdx)`), so the `Map.get(rawIdx)` lookup is the truthful precondition. `isTurnFinalAssistant` was a layered-on heuristic that didn't add safety, it just under-covered.

## Code reference

The map-build at static/ui.js:6378-6382:

```js
for(const entry of renderVisWithIdx){
  const role=entry&&entry.m&&entry.m.role;
  if(role==='user') lastQuestionRawIdx=entry.rawIdx;
  else if(role==='assistant') questionRawIdxByAssistantRawIdx.set(entry.rawIdx,lastQuestionRawIdx);
}
```

And the existing defensive guard inside `_questionJumpButtonHtml` at static/ui.js:395-397:

```js
function _questionJumpButtonHtml(questionRawIdx){
  if(typeof questionRawIdx!=='number'||questionRawIdx<0) return '';
  ...
}
```

So the new gate (`_qJumpTarget !== undefined && _qJumpTarget !== null`) plus the inner guard against `<0` correctly handles the edge case where `lastQuestionRawIdx` is still its seeded `-1` (an assistant message at the top of the render window with no preceding user message yet — e.g. a system-initiated conversation). The button is suppressed, no broken jump.

## One small note

The `null` check in `(_qJumpTarget!==undefined && _qJumpTarget!==null)` is technically redundant — `Map.get` returns `undefined` for missing keys, and `lastQuestionRawIdx` is only ever set to an `rawIdx` (number) or its initial `-1`, never `null`. The `!==undefined` check is sufficient on its own. Not a blocker; the redundancy is harmless and defensive against future map-population changes.

## Verification

A useful manual test for the bug this fixes: trigger a multi-step turn (e.g. a tool-using assistant that does 3+ tool calls before the final answer). Before this PR: only the final assistant bubble shows the ↑ Question button. After: every assistant bubble in the turn shows it, all pointing to the same originating user question. Confirms the symptom in #3114.

For the corner cases I checked:
- First-ever assistant message (no prior user): `lastQuestionRawIdx=-1` → `_questionJumpButtonHtml(-1)` returns empty string ✓
- Live streaming assistant (`m._live === true`): early gate `(!isUser && !m._live)` skips it ✓
- User row: outer gate `!isUser` skips it ✓
- Hidden user message before window: 6373-6377 seeds `lastQuestionRawIdx` from pre-window rows ✓

Minimal, correct, ships. I'd merge this.
